title: The Paper Crown
moral: Humility means doing good without only wanting praise. The best help is the help someone truly needs.

pages.text:
Class Four was preparing for Helper of the Week.

Every Friday, one child received a paper crown for helping others. The crown was yellow, with shiny stars pasted on it.

This week, Arif was sure he would win.

He had arranged the notebooks. He had cleaned the board. He had even reminded Miss Neha about the homework.

"You reminded teacher about homework?" said Zain. "That is not helping. That is danger."

Everyone laughed.

Arif smiled proudly. He liked being noticed.

On Friday, Miss Neha stood in front of the class with the crown.

"This week's helper is... Tanya," she said.

Arif's smile disappeared.

Tanya?

Tanya sat near the back. She was quiet. She had not made big announcements like Arif. She had not carried ten notebooks at once like a hero.

Miss Neha smiled. "Tanya helped Rafi read every day during lunch. She also packed Meena's bag when Meena hurt her finger."

Everyone clapped.

Tanya looked shy. The paper crown slipped over one eye.

"I can only see half the class," she whispered.

The children laughed gently.

Arif clapped, but his hands felt heavy.

At lunch, he saw Rafi reading from a small book. He read slowly, but he did not stop.

"Tanya helped you?" Arif asked.

Rafi nodded. "Every day. She said I should not be scared of big words. She said big words are just small words standing together."

Arif looked at Tanya. She was fixing the crown again because it kept falling.

He suddenly understood.

He had helped where everyone could see. Tanya had helped where someone really needed her.

After lunch, Arif took two paper clips and carefully fixed the crown so it sat properly.

"There," he said. "Now you can see the whole kingdom."

Tanya laughed. "Thank you."

At the end of the day, Arif did not feel jealous anymore. He still wanted to help, but now he wanted to help for the right reason.

The crown was made of paper, but the kindness behind it was real gold.
